classification.difficultyReason: Explain the two selection orders for the same team and captain.

content.prompt:
Suppose a team of four people are chosen from a club with ten members, and a captain is chosen out of the four people chosen.

Explain why $4\times\binom{10}{4}=10\times\binom{9}{3}$.

answer.short: Choose the team, then its captain: $\binom{10}{4}\times4$. Choose the captain, then the other three members: $10\times\binom{9}{3}$. Both count the same teams with a captain.
answer.worked:
Choose the four-person team in $\binom{10}{4}$ ways, then choose its captain in $4$ ways. This gives $4\binom{10}{4}$ selections.

Alternatively, choose the captain in $10$ ways, then choose the other three team members from the remaining nine in $\binom{9}{3}$ ways. This gives $10\binom{9}{3}$ selections.

Each method counts every team with a designated captain exactly once, so
$$4\binom{10}{4}=10\binom{9}{3}.$$
